newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile plans sharp power price cut-Endesa.
newsitem.headline: Chile plans sharp power price cut-Endesa.

text.p: The Chilean government plans to cut electricity generating prices by 11.3 percent in real terms and 8.2 percent in nominal terms, said Endesa CEO Jose Yuraszeck.
The tariffs, which are fixed by the National Energy Commission, will come into force on November 1 and be valid for the next six months.

Yuraszeck said Endesa -- Chile's largest generating company -- is seeking a court order to force the commission to reconsider its decision as it believes the price cut should be 1.5 percent less than the board has proposed.
Endesa's sister company distributor Chilectrica said last week it would also take legal steps to challenge cuts in distribution prices.
Analysts have said they expect distribution prices, which will be set for the next four years, to drop by up to 10 percent.
The commission, Chile's equivalent of an energy ministry, has not given any details publicly of the planned cuts.
Fears over the level of the reduction have sparked a sell-off of Chilean electricity stocks in Santiago and New York in recent weeks, said brokers.
Tariffs have been widely expected to fall sharply to reflect lower fuel costs as the result of the completion of a natural gas pipeline from Argentina next year.
